text:
That the whole face of the world has changed, I would say,

since I heard the steps of your soul move

lightly, oh, very lightly!, beside me, slipping

between me and that terrible edge of death,


so clear, where I thought I would sink; but I was lifted

up to love and could know a new rhythm

to rock life. The cup of bitterness

that God gives us at birth, I will gladly drain,


praising its sweetness, my love, beside you.

The name of lands and the name of sky are altered

according to where you are or may someday be.


And this lute and song of mine, which I once loved

(the singing angels know it well), I love them

only because your name mingles in what they say.

translation.title: That the Whole Face of the World Has Changed, I Would Say
translation.editorial_note: This Spanish variant keeps the altered-world sonnet in a more sentence-driven form.
